name: SGLang: Efficient Execution of Structured Language Model Programs
problem: Complex LLM applications chain many generation calls with control flow, shared state and structured I/O, but serving runtimes execute each call independently and waste the reuse across them.
mechanism: A frontend language with primitives for generation, parallel calls, branching and state, feeding a runtime with RadixAttention: a prefix tree over the KV cache that reuses cached prefixes across requests sharing a system prompt or few-shot prefix, instead of recomputing them.
speedup_reported: Up to 6.4x higher throughput than state-of-the-art inference systems, per the arXiv abstract, on large language and multimodal models across agent control, logical reasoning, few-shot learning benchmarks, JSON decoding, RAG pipelines and multi-turn chat. The 6.4x is a best case over a suite of structured programs; single-turn chat has far less shared prefix to reuse and the gain is much smaller. No baseline engine is named in the abstract itself — read the paper's evaluation section for which systems were compared.

MERGED FIELD BY FIELD - nothing was silently dropped:
  mechanism: the retired record's text was materially fuller (678 chars vs 276) and is RETAINED here rather than discarded. Its text: A frontend language plus a runtime. Frontend provides primitives for generation and explicit parallelism control, so programs are not implicitly sequential. Runtime contributes two optimisations that matter for this slice: RADIXATTENTION, which organises the KV cache in a radix tree over token sequences so a shared prefix across calls is matched and reused rather than recomputed (this is the prefix-reuse mechanism behind agentic multi-turn serving), and COMPRESSED FINITE STATE MACHINES for faster structured-output decoding, which collapses grammar/constraint automaton states into a compact representation so the per-token mask computation on the critical path is cheaper.
  speedup_reported: the two records carried DIFFERENT text for the same paper. This record's text is retained and the retired record's variant is quoted so the difference is visible: "Up to 6.4x higher throughput than state-of-the-art inference systems, across various large language and multimodal models, on tasks INCLUDING agent control, logical reasoning, few-shot learning, JSON decoding, retrieval-augmented generation pipelines, and multi-turn chat.
